title: Add representative workload runners + reporting pipeline v8
author: Priya Kannan
release_notes: Adds v8 of representative workload runners and a new reporting pipeline for nightly benchmark aggregation. Improves profiling baselines and exposes per-workload metrics to BigQuery/S3 for downstream dashboards.
body:
Context and motivation: The Benchmark Lab needs a stable, extensible set of representative workload runners that match common Redwood customer workloads (chat generation, instruction-following, embedding throughput, and reranking). Previous runner versions were fragmented across repos and lacked standardized telemetry and artifactization. This PR consolidates v8 of the runners, adds a profiling baseline harness, and wires a reporting pipeline that publishes aggregated results to our metrics bucket and BigQuery dataset.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds benchmark-lab/representative-runners/v8 with canonical runners for: chat_text_generation, instruction_following, embeddings_stream, and reranking_batch.
- Introduces a profiling baseline harness (benchmark-lab/profiling/baselines) that records latency percentiles, memory/KV cache stats, and kernel utilization snapshots. These are saved as artifacts (json+parquet).
- Adds reporting pipeline (benchmark-lab/reporting/pipeline_v2) that: picks up nightly artifacts, normalizes schema, pushes aggregated metrics to BigQuery table redwood_bench.metrics_v2 and copies raw artifacts to s3://redwood-bench/artifacts/v8/YYYYMMDD/.
- CI: new workflow .github/workflows/benchmark-lab-nightly.yml (disabled by default in main; CI queue job added to verify runners on PRs using a small synthetic workload).
- Perf canary integration: hook added to perf-canary/queries to run a lightweight canary job against representative runner outputs and alert on regression.
- Docs: updates to redwood-docs/benchmark-lab/README.md describing how to run the v8 runners locally and the schema for reporting pipeline outputs.

Implementation notes:
- Runners are python-based and use the existing redwood-sdk-python test harness; they are implemented to be cloud-agnostic (S3/GS storage adapters) and accept a config yaml to pin model variants and quantization profiles.
- The profiling harness uses perf_events and nvprof fallback; we normalize kernel metrics into a compact schema so historical comparisons are feasible.
- Reporting pipeline is implemented as a small airflow DAG that stages artifacts in GCS then runs a normalization job (python) before loading to BigQuery. For non-airflow environments the DAG can be triggered by a lightweight lambda script present in benchmark-lab/reporting/trigger.py.

Checklist:
- [x] Representative runners implemented and smoke-tested locally.
- [x] Profiling harness records examples + artifacts.
- [x] Reporting pipeline normalizes and loads to BigQuery (CI runs against test dataset).
- [x] Docs updated with runbook and schema.
- [x] Added unit tests for normalization code and small integration tests in CI.

Commits (high level):
- feat(benchmark-lab): add representative runners v8 (chat, instruction, embeddings, reranking)
- feat(profiling): baseline harness + artifact format v2
- feat(reporting): airflow DAG + normalization job + BigQuery loader
- ci: add nightly workflow and PR smoke job
- docs: benchmark-lab README + schema docs

Changed files (high level):
- benchmark-lab/representative-runners/v8/chat_runner.py
- benchmark-lab/representative-runners/v8/embeddings_runner.py
- benchmark-lab/representative-runners/v8/reranking_runner.py
- benchmark-lab/profiling/baselines/collector.py
- benchmark-lab/reporting/pipeline_v2/dag.py
- benchmark-lab/reporting/normalize/normalize.py
- benchmark-lab/reporting/README.md
- .github/workflows/benchmark-lab-nightly.yml
- perf-canary/queries/runner_canary.sql
- redwood-docs/benchmark-lab/README.md
- tests/benchmark_lab/test_normalize.py
- benchmark-lab/configs/v8/sample_config.yaml

Testing and CI:
- Unit tests added for normalize.py and collector artifact validation.
- PR CI initially failed on a flaky integration test (tests/benchmark_lab/test_runner_smoke.py) due to a timing-dependent kernel metric; swapped to a mocked kernel provider for CI and retried. Final CI run: all checks green.
- Nightly workflow is gated behind a repo secret and will be enabled by infra for canary runs once this merges.

Review summary and responses:
- Alex Morgan: Asked for clearer schema versioning in artifacts and suggested adding a schema_version field to each artifact. Response: Added schema_version and included compatibility checks in normalize.py.
- Diego Ruiz: Flagged potential cost increase from nightly BigQuery loads. Response: Added a small test dataset in CI and a cost-estimate note in the reporting README; final pipeline includes partitioned loads and a TTL on raw artifacts.
- Nora Patel: Requested an explicit fallback for nvprof not present on some CI runners. Response: Added nvprof fallback and a mock provider for CI (tests stub nvprof).

Reviewer approvals: Alex Morgan (approved), Nora Patel (approved), Diego Ruiz (approved after follow-up commit).

Merge outcome: Squash-merged to main on 2026-02-28 after green CI and approvals.

Notes for operators:
- To enable nightly runs, add the secret BENCH_REPORTING_GCP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT and set the schedule in .github/workflows/benchmark-lab-nightly.yml.
- If BigQuery quotas are constrained, the normalization job supports a --dry-run flag to preview loads.

Related linear tickets: ENG-8271 (representative runners), ENG-9012 (reporting pipeline + baselines).
commits: feat(benchmark-lab): add representative runners v8 (chat, instruction, embeddings, reranking)
feat(profiling): baseline harness + artifact format v2
feat(reporting): airflow DAG + normalization job + BigQuery loader
review_comments: Alex Morgan: Please add schema_version to artifacts so we can support rolling changes. (author reply: added schema_version and compatibility checks in normalize.py)
Diego Ruiz: BigQuery loads look expensive if we don't partition. Can we partition and TTL raw artifacts? (author reply: added partitioning and TTL, updated README with cost note)
Nora Patel: nvprof isn't available on some CI images; add a safe fallback or mock. (author reply: added nvprof fallback and added mock provider for CI)
